name: Grammarly
whatYouLose: Inline suggestions in every text box on every site and desktop app
Low-latency checks without paying per LLM call
Tone detection and organization style guides
prompt:
Build a browser extension writing assistant, a Grammarly alternative using an LLM API.

Stack: Chrome/Firefox Manifest V3 extension in vanilla TS, Harper (WASM) for fast local grammar checks, optional LLM API for rewrites.
Features:
- Underline issues in textareas and contenteditable fields on any site; click to see suggestion and apply.
- Local, instant grammar and spelling via Harper; nothing leaves the machine unless I ask for a rewrite.
- Rewrite menu: shorter, clearer, friendlier, more formal (calls the LLM with my API key stored in extension storage).
- Per-site disable toggle; personal dictionary.
Done when: typing a sentence with an error in a Gmail compose box shows an underline and a working fix.
notes: LLMs made the checking part commodity. Working smoothly in every text field on the internet is still hard engineering.
